rubric_note: Both critics compare computed descriptors against these numbers. Above the flag threshold a candidate proceeds with a caveat; above the fail threshold it is rejected and the designer is told which criterion to fix. The thresholds live in critics.py and are meant to be edited by a chemist.

assumptions.note: Average isolated yield per step. Overall yield is this raised to the number of steps, which is why step count dominates everything downstream.
Process mass intensity contributed by one step at 100% yield — solvents, reagents, water, work-up. Divided by overall yield to give the route's PMI.
Blended cost of everything that goes in, at 10 kg scale: building blocks, reagents, solvent, and its disposal. Scaled for smaller campaigns by procurement_scale_exponent.
Fully loaded cost of one person-day in a kilo-lab, including plant time, analytics and overhead. A CRO quote sits at the top of this range; an academic lab far below.
Charge, react, quench, work up, isolate. Purification is charged separately.
Crystallisation if you are lucky. Chromatography costs more and is charged a premium on top.
Kilo-lab batch size. More product means repeat batches, which is why cost per gram falls sub-linearly with scale.
Operator time for n batches goes as n^exponent: the second batch of the same step is quicker than the first.
Material cost per kg against scale. Buying 10× more material makes it modestly cheaper per kg.
Classical resolution throws away at least half the material and needs a separation; asymmetric catalysis trades that for catalyst cost.
Palladium-catalysed coupling: catalyst and ligand, plus metal scavenging and ICP-MS release testing.
Charged when the structure gives little hope of a crystalline intermediate: silica, solvent and time.
Densely halogenated or unusual-element cores must be bought rather than made, and often cannot be bought at all.
Immobilised enzyme consumed per kg of product in a biocatalytic step, assuming it is recycled a few times.
Screening a panel and, if needed, a round of directed evolution to make one step work on your substrate. Paid once, not per gram.
An enzymatic step that works tends to be high-yielding and selective, which is the point of using one.
Titre of a secondary metabolite in an engineered host after initial strain work. Orders of magnitude of headroom exist here, which is why the cost range is wide.
Working volume of the vessel assumed for a campaign.
Media, utilities, sterilisation, operators and QC for one fermentation, excluding recovery.
Fraction of the titre that survives extraction and purification to isolated compound.
Recovery and purification cost, as a fraction of the fermentation cost it follows.
Pathway assembly, host engineering and titre improvement to reach the assumed titre. Paid once.
Analytical release of the final batch: identity, assay, impurities, residual solvent and metals.
The quoted range is the point estimate divided and multiplied by this. It is deliberately wide: an uncalibrated model with a narrow error bar would be worse than no number at all.

enzyme_classes.replaces: asymmetric reduction of the corresponding ketone, or resolution of the racemic alcohol
enzyme_classes.why: a secondary alcohol is the classic ketoreductase product: reduce the ketone enantioselectively instead of resolving the racemate
a chiral amine on a carbon skeleton is what transaminases are used for at scale; sitagliptin is the textbook case

enzyme_classes.replaces: chemical hydrolysis or classical resolution of an ester
enzyme_classes.why: selective ester hydrolysis or kinetic resolution under mild conditions, with no protecting-group work
converts the nitrile to the acid or amide without the forcing conditions the chemical route needs
enantioselective opening to the diol, and it removes a reactive group the process critic flags anyway

enzyme_classes.replaces: directed ortho-metalation or a protecting-group sequence to install the phenol
enzyme_classes.why: late-stage aromatic hydroxylation avoids carrying a protected phenol through the route, though substrate scope is the limiting factor in practice
removes a coupling reagent and its by-product from the waste stream; newer than the others, so treat as exploratory rather than routine

pocket_method.note: Unoccupied space is found on a grid: a point counts if no receptor atom is within the clash distance, it is enclosed on enough ray axes to be inside a pocket rather than in solvent, and it is clear of the ligand. Connected points are clustered. Geometry only — no energy term, one rigid pose.

docking.note: Rigid receptor, one grid, nine binding modes kept. Scores rank candidates; they are not binding free energies, and Vina is stochastic, so repeat runs of one molecule differ.

target.name: MRP1
target.description: ABCC1, a multidrug-resistance efflux transporter. Blocking it is intended to restore the activity of chemotherapy agents the transporter pumps out of tumour cells.

limitations: The step count is a heuristic from rings, stereocentres and heavy atoms — not a retrosynthesis. No reaction is ever proposed, so no real route is costed.

Cost and time factors are uncalibrated defaults inside published ranges for early-phase manufacture. Nothing here is validated against real process data, so read the ranking between candidates rather than the absolute figures.
Docking is rigid-receptor AutoDock Vina on a single grid. Scores rank; they do not predict affinity.
The property screen applies published rule sets and structural alerts. There is no trained ADMET model anywhere in this project, so nothing here predicts absorption or toxicity.
Building-block availability is approximated from elements and halogen density, not from a supplier catalogue.
The critics are deterministic rules, not a model — deliberately, so every rejection points at a number and a threshold that can be defended or changed.
attribution: Docking: AutoDock Vina. Structure handling: RDKit and Open Babel. Synthetic accessibility: Ertl & Schuffenhauer SA score as shipped with RDKit.
Published activity and analogue data: ChEMBL (EMBL-EBI), CC-BY-SA 3.0, retrieved through the public REST API.
Structural alerts: PAINS (Baell & Holloway) and the Brenk set, both as shipped in RDKit's filter catalogue.
